about: Each card's two roofline ceilings (#109), measured on this box by src/felizjueves/ceilings.py's probes behind the card gate (src/felizjueves/gate.py), and read by src/felizjueves/device.py as Arch.fp64_flops_per_s / Arch.mem_bandwidth_bytes_per_s. A quantity with no record here is NOT CHARACTERISED (0.0): that card has no ridge and gets no verdict. Values are ACHIEVABLE rates (kind), the median over the probe's timed launches, never datasheet peaks. 'published' is the vendors' figures, a sanity bound only (a measured rate above one is a bug in the probe) and the denominator of each record's ratio_to_published; it never reaches device.py. Rewritten only by the opt-in recording run each record's 'command' names.

sm_86.source: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 (GA102) as specified by NVIDIA: 29.8 TFLOPS fp32 at the 1710 MHz rated boost, fp64 at GA102's 1:64 ratio (NVIDIA Ampere GA102 GPU Architecture whitepaper) = 0.465 TFLOPS; 10 GB GDDR6X, 320-bit at 19 Gbps = 760 GB/s.
sm_86.note: At the RATED boost clock. This card's SMI reports a 2100 MHz maximum SM clock and it ran the probe at ~1.95 GHz, so a probe reaching the hardware's issue rate could exceed 0.465 TFLOPS without a bug; the probe's best is ~0.44 (95%), so the bound has not bitten -- if a better probe trips it, check the clock before calling the probe wrong.

gfx1200.source: AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT (Navi 44, RDNA4) as specified by AMD: 25.6 TFLOPS peak fp32 (dual-issue, 3130 MHz boost); AMD publishes no fp64 figure for it, so 0.801 TFLOPS is that fp32 peak at the 1:32 fp64 ratio third-party databases list for RDNA4 (TechPowerUp); 16 GB GDDR6, 128-bit at 20 Gbps = 320 GB/s.
gfx1200.note: fp64 on gfx1200 is slow by design. ASSUMPTION, stated here rather than buried (#116): the derived 0.801 TFLOPS assumes the dual-issue that doubles RDNA4's fp32 peak applies to fp64 too, and AMD publishes nothing that settles it. If it does not, the single-issue fp32 rate is 12.8 TFLOPS and the 1:32 fp64 peak is ~0.400 TFLOPS -- BELOW the recorded 0.446 TFLOPS (112% of it), which would make this bound wrong, not the probe, and would leave the ProbeBug check on gfx1200's fp64 with no bound that bites. Read the recorded value as 56% of 0.801 under the assumption, and as above the single-issue figure without it; either way the recorded ceiling is the measurement and the ridge is computed from it (1.49 FLOP/B), never from this figure.
